title: Python and Qt Tool Development for 3ds Max
purpose: Develop Python and Qt tools for 3ds Max from verified starter templates: MaxScript launcher, safe restart, frameless window with rounded corners and a collapsed bar that follows Max, themed shared controls, Settings / Logs / About / Donate, interface size for 2K and 4K screens, crash-safe start, layered testing and official MaxPkg MZP delivery.

steps: Import this standalone community/custom skill ZIP in a compatible Max Ultra MCP build, then start a new AI chat. It is separate from the product's built-in skills; importing it does not install or run a Python tool.

Ask for Python and Qt Tool Development for 3ds Max. Supply the tool's purpose or existing code, target Max releases, intended scene effects, project destination, the developer name and links to show in About, and a donation link if you want Donate buttons (without one there are none).

New tools start from the included starter templates: one page per module with the full source, renamed to your tool. You get the frameless window with its own title bar and rounded corners, the collapsed bar that docks in the active viewport and follows the Max window, the status bar with Settings, Logs, About and Donate, the controls catalog with Lucide icons, thin pill scroll bars, help balloons, seven editable themes with Warm Graphite as default, and interface size for 2K and 4K screens.

The templates also carry the Max lessons: a start guard that reports a crash at start in the Listener (and so in MaxPkg's log) and starts in safe mode, the garbage-collector hold for 3ds Max 2024, screens looked up by position, background jobs with a GIL pump, heavy work in a child process. Specify your preference for responsive breakpoint adaptation; the assistant asks before enabling it.

For real-Max verification, provide an authorized isolated or synthetic Max fixture connected through Max Ultra MCP. Request the standalone harness with Max's own Python for PySide2 and PySide6, unit, regression and visual checks. Unavailable hosts and unrun scenarios must remain explicitly untested.

Creating a tool includes a package-ready source project and a local installable MZP built by the official MaxPkg Packager through its API in a selected Max instance. Build and archive checks are separate from authorized install/update/uninstall tests. Narrow edits/audits stay scoped; external publication and push require separate authorization.
examples: Use Python and Qt Tool Development for 3ds Max to build a scene report tool for Max 2022 to 2027 from the starter templates. Developer: Jane Doe, link janedoe.example. No donation link. Do not modify scene objects. Deliver the source project and an MZP built with the official MaxPkg Packager.
Move this existing Python Qt tool onto the starter's tool window: own title bar, collapse to the bar that follows Max, Settings with theme and interface size, Logs and About in the status bar.
Apply the controls catalog to this tool: button variants, pills, progress bar, segmented choices, dropdowns, checkboxes, thin pill scroll bars and help balloons, and make it readable on a 4K screen.
My tool crashes 3ds Max 2024 at start for some users. Add the start guard, the Listener report and the garbage-collector hold, and tell me what to ask the users for.

Design isolated tests for this tool's theme switching, repeated launch, collapsed bar following Max, interface size at 125 and 150 percent and 200%+ DPI, using Max's own Python outside Max and available disposable Max instances through MCP.
usage.expectedOutput: For tool creation: a maintainable source project built from the starter templates with a .ms entry point, safe restart, the standard window and controls, Settings / Logs / About (and Donate when a destination is given), themes, interface size, crash-safe start, documentation, layered test evidence, and a locally built official MaxPkg MZP with archive verification; if blocked, the fullest verified ready-to-build project and explicit missing prerequisites. Narrow refactors/audits stay scoped. Includes twelve template pages, seven verified palettes and seven reference screenshots. The templates are verified source to adapt, not a pixel-identical guarantee; no practical Max testing of this skill is claimed.

dependencies: A coding-capable AI client and filesystem access to the tool project; the reference product checkouts are not required after importing this skill.

For generated tools: Autodesk 3ds Max with its bundled Python, pymxs, qtmax and matching PySide/Qt family (PySide2 for 2022-2024, PySide6 for 2025-2027). Inspect actual target versions and capabilities.
For host verification: Max Ultra MCP connected to an authorized isolated/synthetic Max instance. The standalone harness uses the Python that ships with each installed Max outside Max.

For default local MZP delivery: current official maxpkg-dev/max-dev-tool guidance and original packager/hooks, required project metadata and icon/licenses, and a selected suitable 3ds Max connection exposing MaxPkgPackerApi through Max Ultra MCP. No custom ZIP-to-MZP substitute is permitted.
Generated tools need original Lucide SVG icons and their ISC license (the starter lists the icons it uses) and the tool's own brand icon. Icons are not bundled in this instruction-only skill.

A Max Ultra MCP custom-skill importer supporting the optional skill.json display manifest. This package contains instructions, Markdown template pages with source code to copy, JSON palette references and PNG reference images; no executable helpers.

verification.evidence: Catalog importer-contract validation, generated pages, the repository test suite, catalog check and a deterministic ZIP build passed for 1.1.0 and 1.1.1. The starter templates were assembled as one project and run outside 3ds Max with 3ds Max 2022's Python 3.7.9 / PySide2 5.15.1 and 3ds Max 2027's Python 3.13.9 / PySide6 6.8.3: window, help balloon, background job with progress, Settings, About, Logs, collapse and restore, stop; the reference images come from those runs. For 1.1.1 the starter ran again on both bindings with a font scan after a dropdown opened and a button was re-polished twice: no widget at a default size (1.1.0 left the re-polished button at 8.25 / 9 pt). Their parts were host-tested in 3ds Max 2022 and 2027 as TerraScoop. The assembled starter was not run inside 3ds Max, and no practical skill test or reviewer is recorded.
